newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Ethnic fighting erupts in eastern Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Ethnic fighting erupts in eastern Zaire.

text.p: At least 28 civilians have been killed in attacks in Zaire's eastern refugee zone where Zairean soldiers are fighting ethnic Tutsi rebels, humanitarian sources said on Saturday.

A senior Zairean military commander told Reuters that ethnic Tutsi Banyamulenge from Rwanda's army had crossed the border from Burundi on Friday and had targeted civilians living around the village of Kiliba.
"When they arrived they opened fire with light arms on the local population living in villages around Kiliba," he said.
Aid workers in Bukavu said that dead and wounded from Friday's attacks near a sugar factory in Kiliba had been arriving at the area's main town Uvira, 15 km (10 miles) away.
A representative of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees in Rwanda said fighting had erupted near Luvengi refugee camp on Saturday, displacing thousands of refugees.
"Renewed fighting has broken out this morning between the Banyamulenge and Zairean armed forces near Luvengi refugee camp," Paul Stromberg told Reuters in Kigali.
Another aid worker in the Rwandan capital Kigali told Reuters the situation in the eastern Zaire area was very confused and that fighting was heavy.
The Zairean military commander said Kiliba was quiet on Saturday but that Zairean troops were pursuing rebels near Bwegera, about 25 km (16 miles) from Kiliba.

Zaire is host to hundreds of thousands of Hutu refugees who fled fearing reprisals in Rwanda after the 1994 massacres of minority Tutsis by Hutu hardliners there. Other Hutu refugees fled similar ethnic conflict in Burundi.

The Banyamulenge are ethnic Tutsis, some of whom have lived in Zaire for generations. Zaire accuses the Tutsi-dominated army of Rwanda of training and arming Banyamulenge guerrillas to destabilise the region.
The Banyamulenge say they are fighting for their right to Zairean citizenship. They say they are discriminated against by indigenous Zaireans on the basis of language and ethnicity.
Aid workers in Rwanda quoted sources in Uvira as saying Zairean residents had taken to the streets to demonstrate against the Banyamulenge.

The fighting between the Banyamulenge rebels and Zairean authorities trying to drive an estimated 200,000 Banyamulenge from a plateau west of Lake Tanganyika has left Zaire's South Kivu region in a virtual state of war.
Some 220,000 Rwandan and Burundian refugees languish in camps north of Uvira, a town in the delta to the northwest of Lake Tanganyika surrounded by steep hills.
On Friday, up to 26,400 mainly Burundi refugees fled Kagunga camp near Uvira because of the fighting, aid workers said.
The fighting was the second major round in Zaire in a week. Last Sunday about 20,000 Hutu refugees from Burundi fled their camp in eastern Zaire after it was attacked by armed men.
There was no immediate death toll for combatants but the Zairean army commander and soldiers in Bukavu said that no soldiers had been killed.
Zaire has been reinforcing and rearming troops in the area.
